answer: Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the karst history. Churn is counted in fable, and plume publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 21% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Every extra alias adds 10 hours of verification and 7 percent more locked value. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
